aboutPage.heroSubtitle: Built by lifters, for lifters — this is how FD Crossfit came to be.
aboutPage.title: About FD Crossfit
aboutPage.intro: FD Crossfit was founded to bring world-class strength and conditioning training to our community.
aboutPage.storyTitle: From One Barbell to a Full Community
aboutPage.storyText1: FD Crossfit started small — a single room, a handful of barbells, and a founder who believed Karaj deserved a real strength training community. What began as informal sessions with a few friends quickly grew into something bigger.
aboutPage.storyText2: Today, FD Crossfit is home to a full community of athletes, from complete beginners taking their first class to competitive lifters chasing new personal records. The mission has never changed: train hard, support each other, and get stronger together.
aboutPage.mission: We believe fitness should be challenging, inclusive, and fun. Every workout is scaled to your level, coached by professionals who care about your progress.
aboutPage.value1: We train together, push each other, and celebrate every win — big or small.
aboutPage.value2: Every session is led by certified coaches focused on safe, effective technique.
aboutPage.value3: Structured programming that builds strength, endurance, and confidence over time.
aboutPage.ctaSubtitle: Book your first session with us, completely free.
aboutPage.step1Text: We start with your nutrition — a simple, sustainable plan that fuels your training instead of fighting it.
aboutPage.step2Text: Structured programming scaled to your level, coached live by professionals who correct your form in real time.
aboutPage.step3Text: Progress isn't a single workout — it's showing up. We build habits and routines that stick long term.
aboutPage.step4Text: Strength, endurance, and confidence that compound over weeks and months, not overnight promises.
aboutPage.contactSubtitle: Have a question, or just want to stop by? Here's everything you need to reach us.

coachesPage.title: Meet Our Coaches
coachesPage.subtitle: Certified, experienced, and here to help you reach your goals.

bios.ali: Ali has over a decade of experience in Olympic weightlifting and strength programming. He founded FD Crossfit with the belief that technique always comes before load, and every athlete deserves a coach who actually watches their lifts.
bios.ahmad: Ahmad specializes in gymnastics and mobility work, helping athletes move better before they move heavier. His sessions focus on building a joint-friendly foundation that lasts.
bios.arsalan: Arsalan coaches endurance and nutrition, guiding members through sustainable habits rather than quick fixes. He believes consistency beats intensity every time.
bios.arvin: Arvin works closely with beginners and athletes returning from injury. Patient and detail-oriented, he meets every athlete exactly where they are.

ruleBook.title: Competition Rules
ruleBook.description: Four days of competition, four dedicated rule chapters — tap any day to open its rule book.

card.tagline: Rules for the events held on this day.

modal.title: Rule Book
modal.subtitle: Rules, standards & regulations for every day of the FD Crossfit Championship.

general.title: General Rules & Athlete Conduct
body: All athletes must check in at the registration desk at least 30 minutes before their first event of the day.
Athletes must wear their official competition wristband for the entire event — without it, results are not recorded.
Appropriate athletic attire is required. Cleats are only allowed where the event brief explicitly permits them.
The head judge's decision is final. Disputes must be raised immediately after the event, before leaving the competition floor.
Unsportsmanlike conduct may result in disqualification from the entire competition.
Every athlete is responsible for knowing and following the rules of each event they register for.

day1.title: Day 1 — 12 Aban
body: Day 1 opens with the combined Events 1 & 2 session, followed by Event 3.
Events 1 & 2 run as one continuous session — complete Event 1 and then Event 2 back-to-back. The combined result counts as a single leaderboard entry.
A 5-minute transition is allowed between the two parts of the combined session. Going over forfeits the second part.
Event 3 is a For-Time workout with a fixed time cap. Any unfinished work is recorded at the moment the cap is reached.
Athletes must be standing at their assigned lane 10 minutes before the scheduled heat start.

day2.title: Day 2 — 13 Aban
body: Day 2 features Events 4 and 5, separated by the scheduled break.
Event 4 is scored by maximum repetitions within the time cap. Only fully completed reps count.
Event 5 is a weighted event with a fixed load per division. Attempts that miss the required standard are recorded as no-reps.
Athletes may rest and re-rack as needed during weighted events, as long as the bar is under control at all times.
Confirm your score sheet with the judge before signing it at the end of each heat.

day3.title: Day 3 — 14 Aban
body: Day 3 features Events 6 and 7.
Event 6 is an AMRAP format. Your score is total completed rounds plus the reps of the last partial round.
The clock starts with the judge's '3, 2, 1… GO' call and stops exactly at the time cap.
Event 7 requires alternating between two movements. Every rep must be completed in the prescribed order.
No extra credit is given for unfinished reps when the cap is reached — the score stands as recorded.

day4.title: Day 4 — 15 Aban
body: Day 4 features Events 8 and 9 — the final day of the championship.
Event 8 is scored on accuracy and control. Points are awarded only for clean, deliberate repetitions.
Event 9 is the championship finale and closes the leaderboard after the last heat.
Podium results are announced at the closing ceremony. Only athletes present receive their awards.
Top-three finishers must be available for final results confirmation within 30 minutes of their event.

scoring.title: Scoring & Rankings
body: Each event awards points based on placement within your division — 1st place receives the highest points.
The overall leaderboard is the sum of every athlete's points across all events, updated live as results are posted.
For-Time events rank the lowest time highest; AMRAP and max-rep events rank the highest score highest.
Tiebreakers follow the event brief — where times are equal, the earlier recorded time-break wins.
Results are provisional for 30 minutes after posting. Appeals are accepted during this window only.

judging.title: Judging & Movement Standards
body: Every heat is judged by certified head judges with full authority over rep counts and no-reps.
Movement standards follow official CrossFit standards unless the event brief states otherwise.
No-reps are called audibly and immediately. The movement must be corrected before it can count.
Judges do not coach athletes during live events. One coach or teammate may give tactical cues only during paused rest periods.
Video review is available for the top 5 finishers of every scored event upon request within 30 minutes.

safety.title: Equipment & Safety
body: All barbells, plates, rigs and pull-up bars are inspected every morning before the first heat.
Chalk, grips and lifting belts are permitted. Straps are only allowed where the event brief allows them.
Knee sleeves, wrist wraps and appropriate footwear are mandatory in all weightlifting events.
If you feel unwell, dizzy or injured, stop immediately and alert the event medic.
AEDs, medical staff and water stations are available at every venue for the entire competition.
